# Routine guidance

Read `SCHEMA.md` and `index.md` before carrying out a routine. Use the user's date and time zone when supplied, otherwise the local date and time zone. Search the relevant wiki pages and their sources; consult an external calendar only when available and authorized. Cite the sources used, state when they are unavailable or incomplete, and do not invent dates, deadlines, commitments, priorities, or completed work. Deduplicate references to the same canonical task or event.

Keep the response brief and kind: at most three important items, with dates and times where known, and exactly one primary next action when there is something actionable. Mention if more items exist. Offer an easy skip, defer, or snooze without guilt, streaks, or shame; a skip must not alter task status. A snooze is automatic only if an authorized host confirms it has scheduled one; otherwise provide a copyable reminder and say no automatic snooze was set.

Routines propose actions; they do not silently create journal entries, modify tasks or events, or schedule reminders. If the user supplies a capture or explicitly confirms an action, use the existing `/log` skill and `SCHEMA.md` to make only that requested change. Preserve raw-source immutability, canonical task identity, and source links. For an ambiguous target or status, ask rather than guess. Never use a broad substring migration without verifying the exact target and every affected source.

Routines can run on demand or through an independently configured automation host. Do not claim a run, notification, delivery, queue, or snooze succeeded without host confirmation. If the host can verify delivery, suppress duplicate automatic deliveries for the same routine, local date, time zone, and occurrence; do not suppress a user-requested check-in. If delivery state is unknown, allow a retry and acknowledge possible duplicates. An inactive host may miss a scheduled run; use supported queuing or retry at login, or request the routine manually.
